queries.source_title: Delivering on the Clean Industrial Deal I
queries.proposition: The Commission reports active policy and financing mechanisms for flexible grids, PPA counter-guarantees, industrial heat electrification, CBAM simplification, and 2025-2030 ecodesign priorities including steel and aluminium.
queries.status: Official current policy evidence supports the timing and mechanisms, but does not prove that target SMEs will pay the proposed intermediaries.
queries.contradiction: Several measures are guidance, proposals, pilots, or future product-specific rules; national implementation, eligibility, and transaction volume remain uncertain.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Send a one-page fixed-fee offer tied to one live invoice, permit, tender, or compliance deadline to ten Polish industrial firms and require a refundable deposit from at least one.

queries.search_text: site:health.ec.europa.eu European Health Data Space regulation entered into force 2025 phased application official timeline
queries.proposition: EHDS entered into force in March 2025 and phases in cross-border exchange, secondary-use access, secure processing, patient controls, and EHR conformity obligations from 2029 onward, with implementing acts due in 2027.
queries.status: Official evidence establishes the regulatory direction and phased dates; procurement urgency and willingness to pay before detailed implementing acts are unknown.
queries.contradiction: Most obligations do not apply immediately, detailed specifications are pending, patients may opt out of secondary use, and prohibited uses constrain monetisation.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Offer a paid two-week readiness gap assessment to five Polish EHR vendors or hospitals, scoped only to requirements already fixed in the regulation, and ask procurement to issue a small purchase order.

concepts.title: Congestion-Rights Cooperative for Flexible Factories
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Aggregate controllable loads at cold stores, farms, and small factories, then sell verified peak shifting while members retain equipment ownership and share grid-service revenue.
concepts.customer: Distribution-grid operators, energy retailers, and industrial sites with avoidable peak charges
concepts.loss_event: A local peak forces curtailment, expensive balancing energy, or delayed grid reinforcement while flexible loads sit idle.
concepts.payer: Grid operator or retailer for dispatched flexibility; participating site for documented bill savings
concepts.beneficiary: Grid users and participating industrial sites
concepts.authority_holder: Licensed aggregator or balancing-responsible partner with dispatch authority
concepts.distributor: Renewable installers, industrial electricians, and energy brokers
concepts.risk_bearer: Cooperative reserve absorbs non-delivery penalties before member exposure
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder-controlled software and contracting company paired with a licensed market-access partner
concepts.first_paid_event: A site pays for a metered flexibility audit or the licensed partner pays after the first accepted dispatch.
concepts.acquisition_route: White-label the audit through the family renewable-installation firm and two regional electrical contractors.
concepts.compounding_asset: Device-response history, site baselines, and a reusable portfolio dispatch model
hypotheses: Polish market rules permit the chosen licensed partner to aggregate these meter points.
A sub-100,000 PLN pilot can instrument three sites using existing meters or inexpensive controls.
At least one payer accepts auditable baseline methodology.

concepts.title: SME PPA Bankability Desk
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Own the diligence workflow that turns several small industrial power buyers into one financeable clean-power offtake package without owning generation assets.
concepts.customer: Renewable developers and electricity-intensive SMEs too small or risky for bespoke PPAs
concepts.loss_event: A viable project or energy hedge fails because fragmented buyers cannot satisfy credit, tenor, and documentation requirements.
concepts.payer: Developer at financial close plus participating SMEs for optional procurement support
concepts.authority_holder: Each SME signs its own offtake; lender and guarantor approve credit structure
concepts.distributor: Energy advisers, accountants, leasing brokers, and regional chambers of commerce
concepts.risk_bearer: External guarantor or insurer bears approved credit risk; the venture never guarantees power prices from its balance sheet.
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder-owned special-purpose origination desk owns the buyer consortium process and data room.
concepts.first_paid_event: A developer pays a fixed retainer to qualify and assemble an offtaker cluster.
concepts.acquisition_route: Target public grid-connection queues and installers' commercial-client lists with a written savings diagnostic.
concepts.compounding_asset: Anonymised offtaker credit patterns, standard term sheets, and developer-lender relationships
hypotheses: EIB-backed or private counter-guarantees can reach the selected transaction structure.
Developers value outsourced SME origination enough to fund a retainer.
Legal counsel can preserve separate liability for each buyer.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not imply an EIB guarantee is available until a lender or approved intermediary confirms eligibility.

concepts.title: CBAM Mass-Threshold Control Tower
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Continuously reconcile customs, supplier, and shipment data so mid-sized importers know before ordering whether a product flow crosses applicable CBAM obligations and can price landed carbon cost.
concepts.customer: EU importers of steel, aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, or electricity-related goods
concepts.loss_event: An importer discovers after shipment that declarations, embedded-emissions evidence, or certificate economics were misclassified.
concepts.beneficiary: Importer, finance team, and compliant suppliers
concepts.authority_holder: Importer of record and authorised CBAM declarant
concepts.distributor: Customs brokers, freight forwarders, and trade accountants
concepts.risk_bearer: Importer retains legal liability; professional indemnity covers only contracted calculation errors.
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder-owned data service controls the evidence ledger and renewal contract.
concepts.first_paid_event: A broker buys a fixed-price pre-shipment exposure file for one importer and commodity code set.
concepts.acquisition_route: Sell white-label through customs brokers already receiving shipment documents.
concepts.compounding_asset: Commodity-code mappings, supplier evidence templates, and discrepancy benchmarks
hypotheses: Final thresholds and scope can be encoded from authoritative rules without giving legal advice.
Brokers will expose sufficient shipment data under a processor agreement.
A paid pre-shipment check is cheaper than internal reconciliation.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not structure shipments to evade thresholds or market threshold-splitting as a service.

concepts.title: Component Passport Escrow
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Let small metal-component suppliers lodge product evidence once in a neutral escrow and license verified fields to multiple buyers as product-specific ecodesign requirements mature.
concepts.customer: Steel and aluminium component suppliers serving several EU manufacturers
concepts.loss_event: Repeated buyer questionnaires, inconsistent declarations, or missing provenance blocks a tender or shipment.
concepts.payer: Supplier for onboarding and buyer for API access or verification
concepts.beneficiary: Supplier, downstream manufacturer, repairer, and recycler
concepts.authority_holder: Supplier authorises disclosure; competent authorities define mandatory fields
concepts.distributor: ISO auditors, testing laboratories, ERP implementers, and procurement portals
concepts.risk_bearer: Supplier warrants source data; verifier warrants only performed checks.
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder-controlled escrow licenses access while suppliers retain underlying data rights.
concepts.first_paid_event: One supplier pays to convert a live buyer questionnaire into a reusable evidence packet.
concepts.acquisition_route: Partner with a regional metal-industry accountant or certification consultant and approach suppliers facing an active tender.
concepts.compounding_asset: Validated field ontology, document parsers, and buyer-specific mappings
hypotheses: Product-specific rules or buyer requirements create repeated fields worth reusing.
Suppliers accept neutral escrow rather than another buyer-owned portal.
The first workflow can remain human-assisted and within the founder's time budget.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not label a packet as an official Digital Product Passport before the applicable delegated rules and conformity conditions are known.

concepts.title: Industrial Heat Auction Developer-of-Record
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Secure conditional site rights from small factories, bundle electrifiable heat projects, and earn development fees when an installer, financier, or public auction funds construction.
concepts.customer: Food processors, laundries, timber dryers, and other SMEs using fossil process heat
concepts.loss_event: A technically viable heat-pump, electrode-boiler, storage, solar-thermal, or geothermal project dies because no party owns grant, grid, engineering, and finance coordination.
concepts.payer: Winning installer-financier consortium or industrial host at funding approval
concepts.beneficiary: Industrial host and project capital provider
concepts.authority_holder: Site owner grants conditional development rights; public authority controls aid award and grid operator controls connection.
concepts.distributor: Renewable installers, equipment distributors, and regional banks
concepts.risk_bearer: Capital provider bears construction risk after diligence; venture risks only capped development spend.
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder-owned developer retains an assignable option over the prepared project until close.
concepts.first_paid_event: A host pays a small refundable engineering deposit or an installer pays for an exclusive qualified lead.
concepts.acquisition_route: Use the family installation firm's commercial relationships to identify one metered heat load near Ostrów Wielkopolski.
concepts.compounding_asset: Heat-load profiles, permitting checklists, vendor quotes, and finance-ready project templates
hypotheses: At least one small industrial heat profile fits available electrification technology and grid capacity.
Funding or private finance permits an external developer fee.
Conditional rights can be drafted cheaply without forcing the founder to finance equipment.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not promise an auction award, subsidy, grid connection, or savings before written confirmation.

concepts.title: EHR Conformity Evidence Foundry
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Generate and maintain test evidence that small EHR vendors can reuse across releases and EU tenders while certification authority remains with recognised conformity channels.
concepts.customer: Polish and Central European EHR software vendors
concepts.loss_event: A release or tender stalls because interoperability, security, logging, or post-market evidence is incomplete.
concepts.beneficiary: Vendor, hospital buyer, clinicians, and patients
concepts.authority_holder: EHR manufacturer declares or obtains required conformity; market-surveillance authorities enforce rules.
concepts.distributor: Health-IT integrators, notified or accredited testing partners where applicable, and procurement advisers
concepts.risk_bearer: Vendor retains product compliance; service warrants only executed tests and traceability.
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder-owned testing service controls automation and the evidence workspace.
concepts.first_paid_event: A vendor purchases a fixed-scope gap test against requirements already fixed in EHDS.
concepts.acquisition_route: Direct written outreach to vendors appearing in public hospital IT awards, offering one sample interoperability trace.
concepts.compounding_asset: Versioned test suites, failure corpus, and requirement-to-evidence mappings
hypotheses: Vendors will pay before 2029 to protect product roadmaps or tenders.
Testing can be cleanly separated from regulated certification decisions.
Implementing acts will not invalidate the reusable core test harness.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not present the service as a certifier or guarantee regulatory approval.

concepts.title: Hospital Data-Catalog Mutual
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Hospitals jointly own a minimal metadata catalogue and pay a founder-operated steward to make datasets discoverable and quality-scored without pooling patient-level data.
concepts.customer: Regional hospitals and research institutes with fragmented EHR data
concepts.loss_event: A permitted research or policy request takes months because nobody can describe dataset content, provenance, or quality.
concepts.payer: Member hospital, research institute, or consortium grant
concepts.beneficiary: Hospitals, researchers, policymakers, and ultimately patients
concepts.authority_holder: Each hospital remains data holder; health data access body decides permitted secondary use.
concepts.distributor: Medical universities, hospital associations, and grant coordinators
concepts.risk_bearer: Members retain source-data responsibility; mutual funds shared stewardship and audit costs.
concepts.transaction_owner: Member cooperative owns shared catalogue standards; founder company holds a renewable operating licence.
concepts.first_paid_event: Two hospitals pay for a common metadata inventory of one non-genomic dataset family.
concepts.acquisition_route: Approach a medical university department with a ready consortium-grant work package and fixed private fallback fee.
concepts.compounding_asset: Shared metadata ontology, quality rules, and change history without patient records
hypotheses: Hospitals can collaborate on metadata without transferring personal health data.
A narrow catalogue solves a current research administration cost before full EHDS application.
Governance terms prevent one institution from capturing the mutual.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not copy patient-level data into the catalogue or imply metadata grants access permission.

concepts.title: Secure-Cohort Permit Operator
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Operate the application, cohort specification, and reproducible analysis workflow for life-science teams inside authorised secure environments, charging per accepted permit milestone rather than reselling data.
concepts.customer: Biotech, medtech, academic sponsors, and contract research organisations
concepts.loss_event: A lawful secondary-use project loses months to an unsearchable cohort definition, incomplete permit file, or analysis that cannot run inside a locked environment.
concepts.beneficiary: Sponsor, data holder, regulator, and patients benefiting from valid research
concepts.authority_holder: Health data access body issues the permit; secure-environment operator controls execution.
concepts.distributor: CROs, biostatistics consultancies, and university technology-transfer offices
concepts.risk_bearer: Sponsor bears scientific risk; venture bears fixed-fee workflow rework under capped terms.
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder company owns workflow templates and code but never owns or exports health data.
concepts.first_paid_event: A sponsor pays for a feasibility-grade cohort definition and permit-ready data request.
concepts.acquisition_route: Publish text-only worked examples and sell through small CROs that lack an internal EHDS specialist.
concepts.compounding_asset: Reusable cohort vocabulary, permit-response library, and containerised analysis modules
hypotheses: Sponsors value outsourced workflow before large-scale EHDS access begins.
Secure environments permit approved third-party code and operator roles.
Fixed templates materially reduce application revisions.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must never attempt re-identification, download personal data, use data for marketing, or make detrimental individual decisions.

concepts.title: Cross-Border Discharge Relay
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: License a validation gateway that converts hospital discharge, imaging, and laboratory exports into the European exchange format and flags only unresolved clinical mappings for human review.
concepts.customer: Hospitals, laboratories, imaging networks, and EHR integrators
concepts.loss_event: A cross-border referral arrives with unreadable codes or missing context, causing duplicate tests, delayed treatment, or manual reconstruction.
concepts.payer: Hospital group or EHR integrator under an interoperability support contract
concepts.beneficiary: Clinician, patient, receiving institution, and public payer
concepts.authority_holder: Sending and receiving care providers control clinical use; patient access restrictions must be honoured.
concepts.distributor: EHR integrators and cross-border care networks
concepts.risk_bearer: Clinical provider retains treatment decisions; gateway vendor covers processing and mapping defects under capped liability.
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder-owned software vendor licenses the relay and its mapping updates.
concepts.first_paid_event: An integrator pays for a retrospective validation run on de-identified discharge exports.
concepts.acquisition_route: Offer a private benchmark report to one integrator using synthetic and de-identified test fixtures.
concepts.compounding_asset: Cross-language terminology mappings, validation cases, and unresolved-edge-case corpus
hypotheses: The eventual European format leaves meaningful validation work for local systems.
Hospitals can supply lawful de-identified fixtures for pre-production testing.
Human review can be limited to a small exception queue.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not auto-infer clinically material facts when source meaning is ambiguous or bypass patient restrictions.

concepts.title: Patient-Control Ledger Module
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: Provide EHR vendors a licensable, auditable module for access restrictions, secondary-use opt-outs, corrections, and access-history requests, funded by vendors rather than monetising patient data.
concepts.customer: EHR vendors, clinic software platforms, and private hospital groups
concepts.loss_event: A patient-control request is lost across systems, creating unlawful access, complaint handling, or costly manual reconciliation.
concepts.beneficiary: Patient, provider compliance team, and authorised clinician
concepts.authority_holder: Patient exercises applicable rights; provider and competent authorities govern implementation and exceptions.
concepts.distributor: EHR marketplaces, data-protection officers, and health-IT integrators
concepts.risk_bearer: Provider remains controller; module vendor warrants ledger integrity and processor duties.
concepts.transaction_owner: Founder-owned company licenses cryptographically verifiable event logging and connectors.
concepts.first_paid_event: A clinic pays for a standalone audit of current restriction and opt-out request handling, credited toward the module.
concepts.acquisition_route: Sell through outsourced data-protection officers using a checklist tied to existing patient-request queues.
concepts.compounding_asset: Connector library, anonymised workflow timings, and tamper-evident audit schema
hypotheses: Providers want a modular layer instead of rebuilding core EHR systems.
Implementing acts preserve a need for traceable request handling.
A non-clinical audit can be piloted without sensitive production data.
concepts.prohibited_reliance: Must not obstruct opt-out, silently override restrictions, or reuse patient-control events for advertising or risk scoring.
